Let me analyze these teaching examples carefully to identify systematic errors in the forecasts compared to true outcomes.

## Example 1: 2024-09-18
History: Prices drifting lower from ~71 to ~64 over 18 days
Sentiment: Mixed, starting high (1.00) then becoming more negative (0.00, 0.67, 0.33)

Model forecasts: Also drifting lower, starting at 64.17, ending at 64.83
True outcomes: Also drifting lower, starting at 63.70, ending at 64.83

Looking at the differences:
- Model is consistently about 0.4-0.6 points too high (bullish bias)
- At the beginning (day 1-5): Model 64.17 vs True 63.70 ( +0.47)
- At the end (day 26-30): Model 64.54 vs True 64.83 ( -0.29, but model was still slightly too high)

Wait, let me look more carefully. The model seems to be slightly too high (bullish bias) when prices are declining, but the difference narrows as we get further out.

## Example 2: 2024-09-17
Very similar to Example 1, just one day earlier. Same pattern - model forecasts slightly too high (bullish bias) by about 0.4-0.6 points.

## Example 3: 2024-05-02
History: Prices range from ~62 to ~75, including a spike to 74.25
Sentiment: Mixed

Model forecasts: Around 71-75 range
True outcomes: Around 70-76 range

Differences:
- Day 1: Model 72.92 vs True 72.69 (+0.23)
- Day 5: Model 72.52 vs True 71.92 (+0.60)


- Day 10: Model 69.06 vs True 69.19 (-0.13)
- Day 15: Model 74.32 vs True 76.10 (+1.78) - this is a significant error
- Day 20: Model 73.17 vs True 75.20 (+2.03)
- Day 25: Model 71.11 vs True 72.58 (+1.47)
